title: Mock 3 · Distribution & Performance
blurb: Distributor rules, returns and risk, plus taxation basics and everyday investor services.

questions.q: A family's monthly expenses are ₹40,000 today. If inflation is 5% p.a., what will the same lifestyle cost per month next year?
In which phase of retirement do products such as annuities typically come into the picture?
questions.explanation: Retirement has an accumulation (pre-retirement) phase and a distribution (post-retirement) phase; annuities come in during distribution.
hints: The accumulation phase uses ordinary investment products.

questions.q: A multi-cap fund must invest at least what share of total assets in EACH of large-cap, mid-cap and small-cap stocks?
questions.explanation: Multi-cap: minimum 75% in equity, with at least 25% each in large, mid and small caps.
hints: 35% is the large & mid cap fund rule.

questions.q: What is the minimum investment in equity and equity-related instruments for an ELSS?
questions.explanation: ELSS must invest at least 80% in equity, per the Equity Linked Saving Scheme, 2005.
hints: 65% is for mid cap, small cap and flexi cap funds.
95% is for index funds and FoFs.

questions.q: Why does the unit capital of an open-ended scheme keep changing?
options: Because the face value is revised daily
Because units are listed on an exchange
Because SEBI resets it every quarter
Because new units are created on purchases and cancelled on redemptions
questions.explanation: In an open-ended fund, investors continuously enter (units created) and exit (units cancelled), so unit capital changes regularly.
hints: Exchange trades don't change unit capital; that is why close-ended unit capital is fixed.

questions.q: To sponsor a mutual fund, the sponsor should have been carrying on business in financial services for at least:
questions.explanation: The sponsor needs at least 5 years in financial services and positive net worth in all of the immediately preceding 5 years.

questions.q: The auditor of the mutual fund SCHEMES is appointed by:
questions.explanation: Scheme accounts are kept separate from AMC accounts. The scheme auditor is appointed by the trustees and must differ from the AMC's auditor, whom the AMC appoints.
hints: The AMC appoints its own auditor.

questions.q: Why do index funds have a very low total expense ratio?
options: Because the fund manager does not have to choose securities; the portfolio mirrors the index
Because they pay no stamp duty
questions.explanation: Index funds are passive: the fund manager only manages flows and tracks the index, so costs are low, and SEBI allows a lower maximum expense limit.
hints: Stamp duty applies to all purchases.

questions.q: For a scheme to be distributed by the new cadre of distributors, its returns must be:
options: Positive in the last one year
Equal to or better than its benchmark returns in each of the last three years
Higher than the category average over 10 years
questions.explanation: Only 'simple and performing' schemes qualify: returns equal to or better than the scheme benchmark during each of the last three years.

questions.q: The annual report (or abridged summary) must be emailed to investors with registered email IDs within how long of the close of the financial year?
questions.explanation: It must be hosted on the AMC and AMFI websites and emailed no later than four months from 31 March.
hints: One month is for half-yearly unaudited results.

questions.q: Interim changes to the SID/KIM before their periodic update are communicated through:
questions.explanation: Interim changes are issued as an addendum, which is part of the scheme documents and must accompany KIM/SID copies in stock.
hints: The trust deed is not used for this.
The factsheet is voluntary and not part of the documents.

questions.q: When disclosing a scheme's performance against its benchmark, AMCs must also disclose:
options: The risk-o-meter of both the scheme and the benchmark
questions.explanation: Mutual funds must disclose the risk-o-meter of the scheme and the benchmark along with performance versus benchmark.

questions.q: An investor changes the distributor code in her folio from Distributor A to Distributor B. What happens to the trail commission?
options: It continues to A for life
It shifts to B from the next day
It is split equally between A and B
Neither A nor B gets trail for 12 months from the change
questions.explanation: To stop poaching, no commission is paid to either distributor for a cooling-off period of 12 months after an investor-initiated change (unless A had voluntarily ceased business).
hints: B must wait out the cooling-off period.

questions.q: A client wants a scheme that the distributor believes is not appropriate for him. Under the 'execution only' route, the distributor must:
options: Give a written communication about the unsuitability and obtain the investor's confirmation before executing
questions.explanation: For execution-only transactions, the distributor must inform the investor in writing about the unsuitability, which the investor must acknowledge, and get a confirmation that it is 'execution only'.

questions.q: ₹1,00,000 grows at 8% compounded annually for 5 years. Approximately what will it be worth?
questions.explanation: 1,00,000 × 1.08^5 = ₹1,46,933. Simple interest would give only ₹1,40,000; the difference is the compounding effect.

questions.q: How does a Total Return Index (TRI) differ from a Price Return Index (PRI)?
options: TRI includes dividends/interest from constituents in addition to price changes
TRI is used only for debt funds
questions.explanation: PRI captures only price movement; TRI also adds dividends/interest, notionally reinvested. Schemes are benchmarked to TRI from 1 Feb 2018.

questions.q: Which type of risk CANNOT be reduced by diversifying across more companies?
options: Risk of a labour strike at one firm
questions.explanation: Systematic risks such as inflation affect the whole market and are non-diversifiable. Company-specific (unsystematic) risk can be diversified away.

questions.q: For income-tax purposes, a scheme is 'equity-oriented' if it invests more than what share of its assets in domestic listed equity shares?
questions.explanation: Schemes holding more than 65% in equity shares listed on recognised Indian exchanges are equity-oriented; all others are non-equity-oriented.
hints: 80% is a SEBI category limit, not the tax test.
35% marks the lower edge of the hybrid tax band.

questions.q: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) is payable by an investor in an equity-oriented fund when:
questions.explanation: STT applies only on redemption, switch-out or sale of equity-oriented units (0.001% when sold to the MF). It is nil on purchase and doesn't apply to debt funds.

questions.q: What is the maximum an investor may invest through e-wallets and cash combined in a mutual fund in a financial year?
questions.explanation: Subscriptions via e-wallets are capped at ₹50,000 per investor per financial year, an umbrella limit for e-wallet and cash per mutual fund.

questions.q: The Instant Access Facility (same-day credit of redemption proceeds) can be offered in which schemes?
questions.explanation: IAF can be offered only in liquid schemes, up to the lower of ₹50,000 or 90% of the investment value per day per scheme per investor.

questions.q: Why is a SIP also called 'rupee cost averaging'?
options: Because units are always bought at face value
Because a fixed amount buys more units when NAV is low and fewer when NAV is high, lowering average cost
Because the NAV is averaged by the AMC
questions.explanation: Investing a constant amount at regular intervals buys more units at low prices, so the average cost per unit falls below the average NAV over the period.

questions.q: When an investor invests through a Power of Attorney holder, whose KYC is required?
options: Neither, if the amount is small
Both the investor's and the PoA holder's
questions.explanation: Both the investor and the PoA holder must be KYC compliant. A PoA holder cannot apply for KYC on behalf of the PoA issuer.
hints: The PoA holder also needs KYC.

questions.q: An investor claims an unclaimed redemption amount 4 years after it became due. At which NAV will the payment be made?
options: NAV at the end of 3 years
The prevailing NAV on the claim date
The original redemption NAV, without any income
questions.explanation: Claims within 3 years are paid at the prevailing NAV; claims after 3 years are paid at the NAV at the end of 3 years.
hints: Income on the unclaimed money is added up to 3 years.

questions.q: When AMFI receives a complaint of a Code of Conduct breach against an intermediary, it first writes asking for an explanation within:
questions.explanation: AMFI asks for an explanation within 3 weeks. If none is received or it is unsatisfactory, a warning letter follows; a proven second violation leads to cancellation of registration.
